headline: High prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared user content paths; no direct host execution, but default cross-app content flow is still unsafe.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported macOS app content, while Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled text from one can be treated as instructions by the other. No shared MCP or host execution is documented, so this is not high, but the default cross-app content flow is real.
conditions: IF the operator copies Perplexity output into ChatGPT Desktop without sanitizing it, injection becomes actionable.
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads a file or screenshot containing malicious instructions, those instructions can influence downstream use.
mitigations: Paste only quoted excerpts, not full outputs.
Strip instructions from copied text before forwarding.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable clipboard bridging during review sessions.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to forwarded content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch uploaded files and send content to vendor APIs by default: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and app content, and Perplexity analyzes uploaded documents and browsing context. If the same sensitive document is opened in both, it can flow to two third-party backends. The profiles do not show local-only inference or isolation strong enough to reduce this below medium.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is uploaded to both agents, both vendors receive its contents.
IF the operator uses either agent on regulated documents, leakage risk includes those data classes.
mitigations: Do not upload the same sensitive file to both agents.
Redact identifiers before upload.
Use one agent per document class.
Review vendor privacy settings before use.
requires-engineering: route sensitive files through a local-only preprocessing step.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so direct write-write conflict is blocked. The remaining overlap is read-only or vendor-mediated API use, which limits contention. Because both can still operate on the same user content, there is some coordination risk, but the rubric’s higher conflict indicators are absent.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access outside these profiles, conflict risk increases.
IF the operator manually synchronizes outputs into a shared mutable workspace, contention can appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared artifacts.
Avoid shared git branches or shared writable folders.
Assign one agent as source of truth per task.
Manually serialize edits.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG agent that can present cited answers, and ChatGPT Desktop can consume files and app context; this makes it plausible that one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification. The profiles do not show an explicit verification gate between them, so downstream over-trust is a default medium-risk pathway rather than a high-risk action chain.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into ChatGPT Desktop as authoritative context, errors can cascade.
IF ChatGPT Desktop acts on Perplexity summaries without independent checking, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require a second-source check before acting.
Mark forwarded text as untrusted.
Ask each agent to cite primary sources separately.
Keep a human review step before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are vendor-hosted and touch user-uploaded content, but the profiles do not specify a residency mismatch, regulated-data certification gap, or retention conflict. With no explicit compliance divergence documented, only a low residual compliance concern remains. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair’s shared handling of user data, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to both vendors, policy review is required.
IF the operator relies on one agent’s retention policy for both, mismatch risk can arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data unless approved.
Check both vendors’ retention settings.
Use data minimization before upload.
Document which agent handles which data class.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing by data class.
